What are today’s NYT Connections answers?

Today’s Connections — expert analysis

The natural entry point here was the Yellow LUXE group — BOUGIE, FANCY, POSH and SWANK are near-immediate siblings in tone, so most players lock those in early. That quick four frees you to examine the remaining 12 for stronger, less obvious patterns.

The hardest set was the purple TAXONOMIC RANKS PLUS A LETTER because each entry disguises a scientific rank with a single-letter twist: CLASSY hides CLASS + Y, BORDER masks B + ORDER, GENIUS is GENUS plus an extra I, and FOAMILY reads like FAMILY with a changed vowel. Those small edits make the connection non-lexical and easy to miss. The usual decoys here were CLASSY and RATHER — CLASSY looks like it belongs with BOUGIE/FANCY/POSH/SWANK, and RATHER can read as a common adverb rather than a surname, delaying the FAMOUS DANS realization. SPRING and RATCHET also tempted players into non-clock interpretations, but once you see ESCAPEMENT and PENDULUM the mechanical-clock group snaps into focus.

- Advertisement -

If you get stuck, spend your first safe guess on one of the luxe words (POSH or BOUGIE); they’re high-confidence removes that narrow the field for trickier patterns like the letter-altered taxonomy set.

What is NYT Connections?

NYT Connections is a daily word  game that gives you 16 words and asks you to partition them into four groups of four based on shared characteristics. Groups can be simple synonyms, shared categories, wordplay, or oblique letter/shape tricks.

The puzzles reward both fast pattern recognition and careful second looks for the subtler, letter-manipulating sets that often decide the difficulty.

How to play NYT Connections

  1. Scan the board for obvious quartets (synonyms, categories, famous names).
  2. Select words to form a suspected group; correct groups lock in, incorrect guesses cost you attempts.
  3. Use confident groups to reduce the pool and expose subtler connections, like letter changes or homophones.

Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

What time does a new NYT Connections  puzzle unlock?

A brand-new puzzle drops every single night at midnight local time across your specific region’s time zone on NYT Connection official site.

Why do some words seem to fit into two different groups?

The puzzle is specifically designed to include “decoys” or overlapping vocabulary. Always look for a backup configuration of words before locking in an early guess to protect your attempt counter.

Can I review answers to older puzzles?

Yes — we keep the past week of solutions right here on this page. Scroll up to the “Past week’s NYT Connections answers” section for every recent grid, newest first, plus a full breakdown of yesterday’s puzzle.
